roles.title: Incident Responder
roles.description: Lead the response when breaches happen: containment, eradication, recovery.
roles.flavor: Calm in chaos. Clear in crisis.

roles.title: Junior Security Analyst
roles.description: Monitor alerts, triage incidents, and support vulnerability management.
roles.flavor: The best defense is knowing what you're defending.

roles.title: Penetration Tester
roles.description: Simulate attacks to find vulnerabilities before real adversaries do.
roles.flavor: Think like an attacker. Defend like a pro.

roles.title: Security Engineer
roles.description: Build and maintain security tooling, automation, and secure infrastructure.
roles.flavor: Security baked in beats security bolted on.

roles.title: SOC Analyst
roles.description: Detect, investigate, and respond to security incidents in a 24/7 Security Operations Center.
roles.flavor: Every alert tells a story. Most are fiction.

cards.name: Attend SOC Shift Shadow
cards.description: Shadow an analyst through a shift: alert triage, escalation, and handoff procedures.
cards.flavor: Watch how pros separate signal from noise.

cards.name: Complete Partner Security Project
cards.description: Execute the agreed security engagement: pentest, secure code review, or threat model.
cards.flavor: Professional scope. Professional results.

cards.name: Investigate Security Alerts
cards.description: Triage alerts, analyze logs, and determine false positives vs real incidents.
cards.flavor: Signal hides in noise. Find it.

cards.name: Complete Vulnerability Assessment
cards.description: Run scans, manually verify findings, and produce a prioritized remediation report.
cards.flavor: A scanner finds vulns. An analyst finds risk.

cards.name: Deliver Threat Model
cards.description: Produce a structured threat model document with data flow diagrams and risk ratings.
cards.flavor: A good threat model is a roadmap for defense.

cards.name: Run Vulnerability Scans
cards.description: Execute authenticated and unauthenticated scans, validate findings, and prioritize remediation.
cards.flavor: Scanners find vulns. Analysts find risk.

cards.name: Perform Log Analysis
cards.description: Deep-dive into logs to reconstruct attack timeline and identify root cause.
cards.flavor: Logs don't lie. But they do hide.

cards.name: Compete in a CTF
cards.description: Solve challenges in web exploitation, reverse engineering, crypto, or forensics.
cards.flavor: Break it to learn how to fix it.

cards.name: Measure Security Impact
cards.description: Explain how your work improved detection coverage, response time, or security posture.
cards.flavor: Metrics make security visible.

cards.name: Risk Mitigated
cards.description: Partner implemented mitigations for high-risk threats identified in your model.
cards.flavor: Risk accepted, transferred, or mitigated.

cards.name: Partner Security Improved
cards.description: Your work led to measurable security improvements in the partner's environment.
cards.flavor: Fixed in production. Verified in staging.

cards.name: Detection Rule Deployed
cards.description: Your detection rule is in production and generating true positive alerts.
cards.flavor: Rule deployed. Attacker detected.

cards.name: Incident Resolved
cards.description: You helped resolve a real security incident. Document the impact and your contribution.
cards.flavor: Stopped the breach. Protected the data.

cards.name: Document Assessment Learnings
cards.description: Write a post-assessment review: methodology, findings, false positives, and improvements.
cards.flavor: Every assessment sharpens your methodology.

cards.name: Log Security Hours & Reflection
cards.description: Record hours and reflect on alerts investigated, tools learned, and incidents handled.
cards.flavor: Every investigation teaches a new pattern.

cards.name: Threat Model Review
cards.description: Present the threat model to stakeholders and incorporate feedback on risk ratings.
cards.flavor: Alignment on risk enables aligned defense.

cards.name: Create Detection Rule Documentation
cards.description: Document new detection rules: logic, test cases, false positive rate, and maintenance notes.
cards.flavor: Undocumented rules are technical debt.

cards.name: Incident Reflection
cards.description: Write a reflection on an incident you worked: detection, response, and lessons learned.
cards.flavor: Post-incident reviews prevent repeat incidents.

cards.name: Showcase Partner Security Work
cards.description: Present your partner engagement with scope, findings, and remediation guidance.
cards.flavor: Show the risk, not just the vulnerability.

cards.name: CTF Write-up
cards.description: Document your solution path, tools used, and what you learned from each challenge.
cards.flavor: A write-up proves you understand, not just solved.

cards.name: Book SOC Visit
cards.description: Arrange a visit to a Security Operations Center. Confirm date, NDA, and tour agenda.
cards.flavor: See where the alerts come alive.

cards.name: Find CTF Volunteer Role
cards.description: Join a Capture The Flag event or security competition as a volunteer or participant.
cards.flavor: CTFs are the gym for security skills.

cards.name: Threat Model Workshop
cards.description: Facilitate a threat modeling session with the partner: assets, threats, mitigations, and priorities.
cards.flavor: Threat model first. Controls second.

cards.name: Partner Security Requirements
cards.description: Agree on deliverables with an industry partner: pentest, code review, or security architecture.
cards.flavor: Partners need trust, not just tools.

cards.name: Configure Monitoring Rules
cards.description: Create detection rules for SIEM: correlation searches, thresholds, and alert routing.
cards.flavor: Good rules reduce noise. Great rules catch attackers.

cards.name: Confirm Placement Details
cards.description: Agree tasks, dates, and hours with the security team; confirm your mentor and system access.
cards.flavor: Access granted. Trust earned.

cards.name: Complete Security Onboarding
cards.description: Set up SIEM access, configure lab environment, and review security policies.
cards.flavor: Know the environment before you defend it.

cards.name: Understand the Security Brief
cards.description: Clarify the scope: target systems, rules of engagement, reporting format, and timeline.
cards.flavor: Scope creep in security causes real damage.

cards.name: Research Industry Standards
cards.description: Study current best practices, pipelines, and quality bars for your discipline.
cards.flavor: Know the bar before you raise it.

cards.name: Create Personal Learning Plan
cards.description: Map skills to acquire, resources to use, and milestones to hit during the experience.
cards.flavor: A plan turns hope into progress.

cards.name: Set Up Portfolio Tracking
cards.description: Create a system to capture work-in-progress, feedback, and final pieces for your portfolio.
cards.flavor: Document as you go, not after.

cards.name: Establish Communication Routines
cards.description: Agree on check-in frequency, update formats, and escalation paths with your supervisor.
cards.flavor: Communication is a skill, not an afterthought.

cards.name: Define Success Metrics
cards.description: Agree on what "done well" looks like: quality, speed, innovation, or player impact.
cards.flavor: You can't hit a target you can't see.

cards.name: Prepare Questions for Mentor
cards.description: List specific technical, creative, and career questions to maximize mentor sessions.
cards.flavor: Good questions get better answers.

cards.name: Prototype a Core System
cards.description: Build a quick proof-of-concept for a key mechanic, tool, or pipeline.
cards.flavor: Prototypes answer questions designs can't.

cards.name: Collaborate Cross-Discipline
cards.description: Work with a different discipline (art/code/design) to integrate a feature end-to-end.
cards.flavor: Great games are built at discipline boundaries.

cards.name: Optimize a Workflow
cards.description: Identify a bottleneck and implement a faster process, script, or template.
cards.flavor: Automation compounds.

cards.name: Run a Playtest Session
cards.description: Observe players, take notes, and identify friction points in the experience.
cards.flavor: Players reveal what designers miss.

cards.name: Create Technical Documentation
cards.description: Write clear docs for a system, API, or pipeline so others can use and maintain it.
cards.flavor: Documentation is empathy for your future self.

cards.name: Refactor for Maintainability
cards.description: Clean up messy code, rigs, or files to improve readability and reduce future bugs.
cards.flavor: Clean craft enables speed.

cards.name: Record Peer Feedback
cards.description: Document specific feedback from teammates and how you acted on it.
cards.flavor: Feedback implemented is growth demonstrated.

cards.name: Capture Before/After Comparison
cards.description: Show side-by-side evidence of improvement: performance, quality, or player experience.
cards.flavor: Visual proof needs no translation.

cards.name: Write a Case Study Outline
cards.description: Structure a portfolio case study: problem, process, solution, result, reflection.
cards.flavor: Case studies get you hired.

cards.name: Collect Quantitative Metrics
cards.description: Gather data: frame rates, load times, player retention, iteration speed, bug counts.
cards.flavor: Numbers convince skeptics.

cards.name: Document a Failure & Recovery
cards.description: Record what went wrong, root cause analysis, and the fix that prevented recurrence.
cards.flavor: Failures documented become wisdom.

cards.name: Create a Showcase Video/GIF
cards.description: Record a 30-second clip of your work in context: in-engine, in-game, or in-pipeline.
cards.flavor: Show, don't just tell.

cards.name: Feature Adopted by Team
cards.description: Your prototype, tool, or process was adopted as standard practice by the team.
cards.flavor: Adoption is the ultimate validation.

cards.name: Mentored a Peer
cards.description: Helped another student/junior improve their skills through guidance and knowledge sharing.
cards.flavor: Teaching proves mastery.

cards.name: Contributed to Shipped Content
cards.description: Your work is part of content that reached players, even in a small way.
cards.flavor: Shipped is the only metric that counts.

cards.name: Wild Card: Industry Veteran Insight
cards.description: A veteran shares hard-won wisdom. Use in place of any Setup, Action, or Proof card for any set.
cards.flavor: Experience is the best teacher.

cards.name: Wild Card: Cross-Discipline Workshop
cards.description: An intensive workshop bridges disciplines. Use in place of any card for any set.
cards.flavor: Boundaries are where innovation lives.

cards.name: Wild Card: Personal Project Sprint
cards.description: A focused personal project fills a gap. Use in place of any card for any set.
cards.flavor: Self-directed work shows drive.

sets.name: Block Placement
sets.why: A placement gives practical experience and, if it goes well, an employer reference.

sets.name: Employer Visit
sets.why: A visit builds industry understanding and useful contacts.

sets.name: Volunteering
sets.why: Volunteering shows reliability, initiative and teamwork.

sets.name: Live Project Brief
sets.why: A finished brief creates a portfolio piece that shows you can respond to a client's needs.

sets.name: Industry Partnership
sets.why: A partnership gives you specialist feedback and experience working with professionals.
